modern: You are a little soul carrying around a corpse, as Epictetus used to say.
original: Thou art a little soul bearing about a corpse, as Epictetus used to say.

explained.summary: Epictetus, the former slave turned Stoic teacher whose ideas shaped Marcus, liked to say that you are a little soul carrying around a corpse. It’s a deliberately stark image. Your body is already mortal matter, and what really makes you you is the mind that carries it.
